scope: One actual ModelOpt calibrated-global group16 NVFP4 W4A4 artifact and its fixed producer source. No product implementation or whole-artifact support claim.

artifact.quartet: U8[N,K/2] adjacent low-first codes; F8_E4M3[N,K/16] group scales; independent F32 scalar weight_scale_2 and input_scale.

findings: The saved dynamic=false metadata describes calibrated global input scaling. The pinned producer still computes block scales from the current activation absmax for each16-value block, rounds normalized scales to E4M3, then quantizes activations to E2M1. It must not be interpreted as static per-block activation scales.

Current group32 power-of-two FP4 roundtrip, group32 FP4 weights plus dynamic FP8 activation, GGUF NVFP4 and CT local-dynamic W4A4 are distinct contracts. Existing naming does not establish a product entry for this artifact.

Pinned non-fast weight decode forms group_scale*global_scale before applying the FP4 value; the fast kernel expresses FP4*group_scale then global_scale. This research does not certify these two rounding trees as equivalent.

The proposed explicit linear entry keeps packed banks and two-level scales, quantizes current activation once, and decodes bounded weight groups/tiles through existing provider/Graph ownership. This is a repair proposal, not completed code.
limitations: Original weight codes, scale scalar values and model tensor payloads were not read; only the complete safetensors header and8-byte length prefix were read.
No product operator, kernel, model, numerical quality, throughput or memory experiment ran.
The exact declared operand narrowing/accumulation/scale multiplication order needs selection and actual regression before claiming implementation or artifact equivalence.
The pinned fake-quant reference includes its own small-scale guard; do not infer a different consumer/hardware path is identical from metadata alone.
This does not establish CT local-dynamic or GPTQ packing/zero-point/index compatibility.

archive.excluded: No weight/scalar tensor payloads, SDK, object, executable, native binary or copied cache.
